newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia lumber labor talks seen resuming.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia lumber labor talks seen resuming.

text.p: Wildcat strikes at International Forest Products Ltd could end as early as Friday evening, paving the way for a restart of labor negotiations for British Columbia's lumber industry.
Sonny Ghag, president of the IWA-Canada local union for the area east of Vancouver, said talks were underway in an attempt to persuade the strikers to end the job action.
"I'm hopeful that before the end of the day we'll get them back and would hope they (the plants) would be in operations by tonight or Monday, hopefully tonight," he said.
Forest Industrial Relations, which bargains on behalf of 65 forest companies, has applied to the provincial Labor Relations Board for an order ending the job action.
The wildcat strikes broke out at Interfor facilities in the lower mainland of British Columbia on Friday morning after the forestry company announced plans to close its McDonald sawmill.

After learning of the strikes, Forest Industrial Relations cancelled negotiations with the IWA-Canada on a new labor contract for the coastal lumber industry and refused to resume talks until the action ended.

Sources said that if the strikes end, negotiations could resume on Tuesday, but there were no meetings scheduled yet. Despite a disagreement between the two sides over wages, officials have said a contract deal was within reach.
